issue: After Kisor v. Wilkie, how much deference, if any, should a court give to the Sentencing Commission's commentary to the Guidelines?

sides.position: Applies the Kisor two-step framework: the commentary gets deference only if the guideline is genuinely ambiguous after traditional tools of construction, and then only if the agency's reading is reasonable and warrants controlling weight.
cases: United States v. Castillo, 69 F.4th 648 (9th Cir. 2023)
United States v. Mendonsa, No. 25-1517 (9th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: Takes a different approach to deference owed to Guidelines commentary after Kisor. The excerpt does not describe this position.

this_court: Applies the Kisor framework, following Castillo (9th Cir. 2023).
quote: Although the circuits disagree over the deference owed to the Guidelines commentary after Kisor, this court applies the Kisor framework.
cite: United States v. Mendonsa, No. 25-1517 (9th Cir. 2026)
